Current Date & Spring Kickoff

Today is Friday, March 27, 2026. Let's shift gears from Core Java to the Spring Framework—the backbone of modern enterprise Java applications.

1. What is the Spring Framework?

Spring is a lightweight, integrated framework used to build enterprise-level applications. Its core features are Dependency Injection (DI) and Inversion of Control (IoC), which help create loosely coupled code.

2. What is Inversion of Control (IoC)?

IoC is a design principle where the control of object creation and lifecycle is handed over to the framework (the IoC Container) instead of the developer manually using the 'new' keyword.

3. Dependency Injection (DI)

DI is the implementation of IoC. It allows a class to receive its dependencies from an external source (Spring Container) rather than creating them internally.

4. BeanFactory vs. ApplicationContext

Both are IoC containers. BeanFactory is basic and uses lazy loading. ApplicationContext is advanced, supports eager loading, AOP, and internationalization, making it the standard choice.

5. Spring Bean Scopes

Singleton: One instance per container (default). Prototype: New instance every time. Others include Request, Session, and Application for web apps.

6. What is @Autowired?

This annotation tells Spring to find a matching bean in the container and 'inject' it into the field, setter, or constructor automatically.
code:
@Autowired
private Repository repo; // Spring 'wires' this bean here

body:
7. @Component vs @Service vs @Repository

@Component: Generic bean. @Service: Business logic layer. @Repository: Data access layer (with automatic exception translation). All are candidates for auto-scanning.
code:
@Repository
public interface UserRepo extends JpaRepository<User, Long> { }

body:
8. Spring Bean Lifecycle

The steps a bean goes through: Instantiation -> Populate Properties -> Aware interfaces -> PostProcessors -> Initialization -> Destruction.

9. What is Spring AOP?

Aspect-Oriented Programming separates 'cross-cutting concerns' (like logging or security) from actual business logic. It uses 'Aspects' to intercept method calls.

10. Core Spring Modules

Spring is modular. Key modules include Spring Core (DI/IoC), Spring AOP, Spring MVC (Web), Spring DAO/ORM (Database), and Spring Boot.
code:
// You only import what you need in pom.xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
</dependency>

body:
Today's Focus: Spring Boot Mastery

Today is Friday, March 27, 2026. We are moving from the core framework into Spring Boot—the opinionated layer that simplifies everything.

1. What is Spring Boot?

Spring Boot is an extension of the Spring framework that eliminates 'boilerplate' configuration. It aims for Rapid Application Development by providing default 'opinions' for your project setup.
code:
// No XML, no complex setup.
// Just a POM and one Main class.

body:
2. What is Auto-configuration?

Spring Boot looks at your classpath. If it sees `h2.jar`, it automatically configures an in-memory database. If it sees `spring-webmvc`, it sets up a DispatcherServlet. It 'guesses' what you need.
code:
@EnableAutoConfiguration 
// Usually included in @SpringBootApplication

body:
3. Spring Boot Starters

Starters are a set of convenient dependency descriptors. Instead of adding 10 different jars for Web development, you just add one `spring-boot-starter-web` and it pulls the rest.
code:
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
</dependency>

body:
4. @SpringBootApplication breakdown

This is a 'triplet' annotation. It combines @Configuration (tags class as a source of beans), @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan (looks for components in the package).
code:
@SpringBootApplication 
// = @Configuration + @EnableAutoConfiguration + @ComponentScan

body:
5. Embedded Servers

Unlike traditional Spring, Spring Boot packages the server (Tomcat, Jetty, or Undertow) inside the JAR. You don't need to install a server on your machine; you just run the JAR.
code:
java -jar my-app.jar 
// Starts Tomcat on port 8080 by default

body:
6. Spring Boot Actuator

A sub-project that provides 'production-ready' features. It allows you to monitor your app, check health, view metrics, and see environment variables via HTTP endpoints.
code: // Access via: /actuator/health or /actuator/metrics

body:
7. application.properties vs .yml

Spring Boot supports both. Properties are flat key-values, while YAML is hierarchical and more readable for complex configurations. YAML is often preferred in modern microservices.
code:
server:
  port: 8081
spring:
  profiles:
    active: dev

body:
8. Spring Boot Profiles

Profiles allow you to separate parts of your application configuration and make it only available in certain environments (e.g., `application-dev.yml` vs `application-prod.yml`).

9. @RestController vs @Controller

@Controller is for web pages (returns a View). @RestController is a shortcut for @Controller + @ResponseBody, used for REST APIs that return data (JSON/XML).

10. @Value vs @ConfigurationProperties

@Value is good for single properties. @ConfigurationProperties provides 'strong typing' and allows you to map entire groups of properties to a Java object.

11. DevTools

A module that improves the development experience. It provides Auto-restart (restarts app when code changes) and LiveReload (refreshes the browser automatically).
code:
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-devtools</artifactId>
</dependency>

body:
12. Exception Handling: @ControllerAdvice

Instead of try-catch blocks everywhere, you use a global class to catch exceptions across all Controllers and return a consistent Error Response.

13. Command Line Runner

An interface used to indicate that a bean should run specific code immediately after the application context is loaded. Great for seeding test data.

14. Customizing the Banner

Spring Boot allows you to change the ASCII art that prints on startup. Just place a `banner.txt` file in your `src/main/resources` folder.
code:
// Inside banner.txt
// CODE CAST VERSION 1.0

body:
15. Spring Boot Testing

@SpringBootTest starts the entire application context for integration tests. For faster unit tests, you can use @WebMvcTest or @DataJpaTest to only load specific layers.

Current Date & Advanced Focus

Today is Friday, March 27, 2026. We are diving into the world of Data Persistence and Distributed Systems.

1. What is Spring Data JPA?

It is a part of the Spring Data project that makes it easy to implement JPA-based repositories. It reduces the amount of boilerplate code required to interact with databases by using Repositories.

2. Derived Query Methods

Spring Data JPA can 'parse' method names to generate SQL queries automatically. As long as you follow the naming convention, you don't need to write JPQL or SQL.
code:
// Generates: SELECT * FROM users WHERE email_address = ?
User findByEmailAddress(String emailAddress);

body:
3. @Transactional Annotation

This annotation ensures that a series of database operations are treated as a single unit. If any operation fails, the entire transaction is rolled back to maintain data integrity.

4. The N+1 Select Problem

A performance issue where the app executes one query to fetch 'N' parent records and then 'N' additional queries to fetch child records. Solved using Join Fetch or Entity Graphs.
code:
@Query("SELECT u FROM User u JOIN FETCH u.roles")
List<User> findAllWithRoles();

body:
5. Lazy vs Eager Loading

Lazy: Child objects are loaded only when accessed. Eager: Child objects are loaded immediately with the parent. Lazy loading is generally preferred to save memory.
code:
@OneToMany(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
private List<Address> addresses;

body:
6. What are Microservices?

An architectural style where an application is built as a collection of small, independent services. Each service runs its own process and communicates via lightweight protocols like HTTP/REST.
code: // Scalable, Independent, and Tech-agnostic

body:
7. Service Discovery (Eureka)

In a microservice environment, service instances change frequently. Eureka acts as a phonebook where services register themselves so others can find them by name.
code:
@EnableEurekaServer
// Enables the discovery registry

body:
8. API Gateway

The single entry point for all clients. It handles routing, security, rate limiting, and monitoring, protecting the internal microservices from direct external exposure.

9. Circuit Breaker Pattern

Prevents a failure in one service from cascading to others. If a service is down, the 'circuit' opens and returns a fallback response immediately instead of waiting for a timeout.
code:
@CircuitBreaker(name = "userService", fallbackMethod = "defaultUser")
public User getUser(String id) { ... }

body:
10. Feign Client

A declarative REST client that makes writing web service clients easier. You simply define an interface and Spring Cloud provides the implementation.

11. Spring Security: JWT

JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are used for stateless authentication. The server issues a signed token to the client, which the client sends back in the Authorization header for every request.
code: // Authorization: Bearer <token>

body:
12. @Cacheable

Allows you to cache the result of a method. If the method is called again with the same parameters, Spring returns the value from the cache instead of executing the method.
code:
@Cacheable("products")
public Product getProduct(Long id) { ... }

body:
13. Bean Validation (@Valid)

Standard way to validate incoming data. You annotate your DTO fields with constraints like @NotNull or @Size, and Spring returns a 400 error if validation fails.
code: public ResponseEntity save(@Valid @RequestBody UserDTO user) { ... }

body:
14. RestTemplate vs WebClient

RestTemplate: Synchronous/Blocking (older). WebClient: Reactive, non-blocking, and part of Spring WebFlux. WebClient is the modern recommendation.
code:
webClient.get().uri("/url").retrieve()
        .bodyToMono(String.class);

body:
15. Externalized Configuration

Using Spring Cloud Config, you can store your application settings (like DB passwords) in a central Git repository. Services fetch their config at startup.
code: spring.config.import=configserver:http://localhost:8888
